To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the classical dynamics is determined by a Lie algebra of Poisons Brackets on the manifold of fields, while the quantum dynamics is determined by an analogous Lie algebra of commutation relations on the manifold of operators, 2) the classical and quantum manifolds are both isomorphic to the manifold of functions on the phase space, and 3) the quantum manifold can be obtained from the classical one by the process of quantization, which is a nonlinear deformation of the classical manifold.

(a) QM is a nonlinear reformulation of Heisenbergs’ dynamics, (b) the nonlinearity of this reformulation is due to the presence of a nonlinear term proportional to a constant (Planck’s constant), which is a measure of the deviation of QM from CM and (c) this nonlinearity can be removed by a nonlinear transformation of the observables, which is a nonlinear generalization of the linear unitary transformations used in QM.
